title: European Commission hit by cyberattack affecting staff payroll and leave systems
date_note: Date of the report; Politico, relayed by Izvestia, says the attack had been going on for more than 10 days.
summary: Commission spokesperson Thomas Regnier confirmed an AI-generated cyber campaign, detected 22 October, which he called misuse of a publicly available AI tool he did not name. Several applications were taken down and most have been restored; Sysper and MyPMO were reported affected. He said no evidence of a data breach affecting staff as a whole has been detected. Per Politico, CERT-EU linked the tool ARTEX.
plain: The European Commission confirmed an AI-generated cyber campaign against it. It took several applications offline as a precaution and most are back. It has found no evidence of a data breach affecting staff as a whole.
exec: An AI-generated campaign hit an EU institution; the Commission says it has detected no evidence of a data breach affecting staff as a whole.
action: If you work with EU institutions, expect notices from them and treat unexpected messages claiming to be from Commission staff with care.
impact: Several applications taken down as a protective measure, most since restored (Regnier); Sysper and MyPMO reported offline, restored early in the week of 16 Nov (heise); salaries paid as usual; no evidence of a data breach affecting staff as a whole detected, investigation ongoing (Regnier).

sources.name: The Telegraph via Yahoo News (relaying Politico)
Help Net Security (relaying the Commission briefing and Politico)

validation.note: Euronews (own anonymous official; Sysper and JSIS named) and Politico (relayed by Izvestia, Telegraph, Anadolu, La Libre) report independently; the Commission has not confirmed the scope. Politico original not read. 20 Nov: Security Affairs (19 Nov) reports CERT-EU named ARTEX as a possible tool and more than ten days of disruption; CERT-EU and Politico originals not read. 20 Nov: Help Net Security reports spokesperson Regnier confirming an AI-generated campaign at the Commission midday briefing; ARTEX link is Politico, not Commission; originals not read.
